event.summary: old tmux terminal retirement loses retained history and ends programs, explicitly accepted
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

TLDR: Upgrading a supervisor with sessions still in old tmux terminals ends their programs and discards their retained terminal history; a later Restart starts with an empty terminal.

Details: The assigned host_restart.rs patch removes tmux_restart_seed and Replacing::TmuxWindow, including the old history-preserving migration and fallback. At this revision service/core/old_terminals.rs:159-168,176-233 ends the old private tmux server, while host_restart.rs now handles only a HostTerminal or no terminal. Source review establishes this removal is deliberate rather than an accidental loss of the migration path. SPEC_impl.md, Terminal substrate: private tmux server, lines 2882-2884 says: "This release ends them at startup (below); every terminal runs in a terminal host". SPEC.md, Lifecycle operations, lines 1945-1947 says: "When the terminal no longer exists (the process that kept it ended, after a reboot, or an old terminal this release ended, see [Terminal experience](#terminal-experience)), Restart starts with an empty one." SPEC_impl.md:2919-2925 explicitly accepts startup proceeding after failures and even a second agent after Restart; this record concerns only the deliberate removal of tmux migration, not independent defects in startup cleanup.

Suggested bucket: highest (programs and retained history can be lost). Could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed through source and contract analysis; no execution. proposed_drop: explicitly accepted old-terminal retirement and empty Restart under the exact specification text cited above; independent drop check required. possible_cover: the cited specifications only; no queue or excluded coverage sources searched. Material caveat: live terminal hosts retain their normal restart history-seeding path; this consequence is limited to the retired tmux substrate.

event.summary: old tmux terminal retirement loses retained history and ends programs, explicitly accepted
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

TLDR: Upgrading a supervisor with sessions still in old tmux terminals ends their programs and discards their retained terminal history; a later Restart starts with an empty terminal.

Details: The assigned patch removes tmux_restart_seed, Replacing::TmuxWindow and the tmux seed's CancelOnDrop. old_terminals.rs:159-168,176-233 ends the old private server. host_restart.rs:199-219 handles a held host runtime or none and defaults to no seed. core.rs:12486-12493 reads the held host's seed before claiming the new generation, and 13000-13028 forwards that runtime and seed.

Literal specification acceptance: SPEC.md, Terminal experience, 3006-3010: "This release ends them: the first time a host's supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program." At 3013-3016: "A failure to end the server or to stop what ran there is logged and never stops the supervisor from starting; those sessions are treated as ended all the same, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running. After an update to this release, Restart, Clone and Replace start such a session in a new, empty terminal." SPEC.md, Lifecycle operations, 1945-1947 also accepts an empty Restart after an old terminal this release ended; SPEC_impl.md:2880-2932 describes retirement and its failure residuals.

Synthesis source checks: Removing the tmux-specific CancelOnDrop does not remove the retained host seed's ownership/cancellation mechanism. hosts/terminal.rs:2443-2450 sends the seed request to the existing runtime; 3155-3161 handles it there. seed_now at 3733-3766 owns the blocking encode, uses the runtime's cancel token, and brings the emulator home even if the request's answer receiver disappears. host_restart.rs:418-490 waits for settled output, requests MAX_SNAPSHOT, and refuses a missing seed during supervisor stopping. host_restart.rs:294-387 publishes the new host before ending the old one; core.rs:12805-12807 bypasses restoration after publication. Definitive restoration at 12933-12948 retains the previous host under publishable; ambiguous restoration names no terminal and aborts the previous runtime. These checks establish preservation of these specific host-seed/caller contracts, not blanket correctness of every failure path; l1 separately records an unchanged unwind-policy concern.

Suggested bucket: highest, unchanged (programs and retained history can be lost). Could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed by source/contract analysis; no execution. proposed_drop: literal specification acceptance of deliberate retirement and empty Restart only; independent drop check still required and no parent drop accepted. possible_cover: parent reports likely duplication with g053/f1, not independently read/matched here.

Material caveats: This proposal does not settle misleading survival guidance (distinct g004/g071 concerns identified by parent), hidden failure warnings (g033), or independent startup cleanup bugs. Those require their own trigger/consequence analysis. The retained host seed was checked in source; nothing was reproduced or observed at runtime.

event.summary: tab settle probe conversion preserves failure handling
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

TLDR: Considered whether tab opens could accept a dead or unreadable shell after the process-probe enum changed. Source refutes a behavior change.

Details: host_tabs.rs:714-727 retains host.probe()? and maps Dead to refusal, Running to waiting, and Gone to an error. The same-commit hosts/terminal.rs HostStatus::probe diff (around lines 800-835) maps exactly the old Owned{dead:false,pid:Some} result to Running(pid), the old Owned{dead:true,pid:None} to Dead, retains Gone and the errors for an unavailable host or failed pinned-child check. ForeignOwner was never emitted by the host probe and its removal here loses no case. service/core.rs:14120-14142 still derives sweep roots from HostTerminal::sweep_root, and hosts/terminal.rs:2557-2583 rechecks the pinned start identity. SPEC_impl.md, Terminal host / Tabs in hosts, requires a dead-at-open refusal and refusal for a host that cannot be read.

Suggested bucket: other, no established user impact. Could-be-highest: no; no unsafe kill root or new loss route established. Confidence: confirmed through source comparison, no execution. proposed_drop: refuted by the one-to-one host probe mapping and preserved error propagation. possible_cover: none. Caveat: this checks the assigned caller conversion, not independent defects in host liveness implementation.

event.summary: tab reply no longer carries terminal kind under the new protocol
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

TLDR: Considered whether removing the tab terminal kind leaves clients unable to choose the right renderer. The same revision intentionally removes that choice and advances the protocol.

Details: host_tabs.rs:169-172 now returns TabInfo{id}. crates/farhelm-proto/src/lib.rs:1676-1695 declares that exact shape and requires only a tab identity, with stable creation order supplying its positional label. Its same-commit diff at line 255 advances PROTOCOL_VERSION from 76 to 77. SPEC_impl.md:3015 states: "Protocol 77 removed the byte streams with the old terminals and xterm.js: every attachment's data channel carries" a grid stream (full surrounding contract still being checked in this pass). All served terminals are hosts under the immediately preceding retirement change; no remaining kind should be emitted by this helper.

Suggested bucket: other, no established user impact. Could-be-highest: no; this considered issue is renderer/protocol compatibility, not a destructive target or kill decision. Confidence: confirmed for this assigned reply change by source and schema comparison; no execution. proposed_drop: refuted by the coordinated TabInfo schema removal and protocol version bump. possible_cover: none. Caveat: this does not independently review all changes to protocol dispatch or the grid renderer, which belong to other groups.

event.summary: tab reply kind removal is coordinated; old-page breakage is explicitly accepted
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

TLDR: Removing the terminal kind is safe for matching clients. A page left open from the previous release can misdraw a terminal and lose its attachment on input until reloaded; the specification explicitly accepts that consequence.

Details: host_tabs.rs:169-172 now returns TabInfo{id}. crates/farhelm-proto/src/lib.rs:1676-1695 declares that exact shape, using stable creation order for positional labels. Its same-commit diff at line 255 advances PROTOCOL_VERSION from 76 to 77. SPEC_impl.md, Grid streams, lines 3010-3031 says: "every attachment's data channel carries a grid stream" and "SessionInfo and TabInfo no longer report a terminal kind". Matching peers need no renderer choice. The full surrounding contract read at 2985-3050 explicitly says: "A page loaded from the previous helm and left open across the update must be reloaded; nothing keeps it working." It explains that an old page can take the absent kind and stream notice for an old byte stream, display grid messages as output, and have typing rejected as malformed input. Its final decision is: "Keeping the stream notice for such pages was considered and not done: a reload is the whole remedy." A mismatched helm and supervisor refuse at hello; this exception is the already-loaded page.

Suggested bucket: high for the established stale-page display/input interruption, other for the refuted matching-client concern. Could-be-highest: no; the considered route displays messages wrongly and rejects input, with no source route to a destructive action or loss of user-owned work established. Confidence: confirmed through source/schema comparison and the explicit contract; no execution. proposed_drop: matching-client regression refuted by coordinated schema/protocol changes; old-page consequence explicitly accepted by the exact Grid streams text above. possible_cover: the cited specification only; no excluded coverage sources searched. Caveat: the stale-page consequence is documented by contract, not independently observed in execution; broader protocol/renderer implementation belongs to other groups.

event.summary: tab cleanup preserves scope provenance, host end checks and restart sharing
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

TLDR: Considered whether replacing the tab-scope wrapper with a boolean and removing the detach result lets closing a tab falsely report cleanup complete, or lets an agent Restart lose its tab runtimes. Source refutes those specific regressions.

Details: Removed HostTab::tab_scope exactly mapped self.scoped to Scoped/Unscoped. host_tabs.rs:405-417 records the actual launch's scope selection in the tag/cell; failed starts pass the same scoped at 424-427. Close passes tab.scoped at 987 and 1004-1011. core.rs:14120-14180 takes a pinned child root before teardown, passes ScopeKillFailure::Refuse, and uses MarkerOnly after host teardown. sweep.rs:1291-1300 maps a scoped tab into recorded units, an unscoped tab into derived units with a required portable sweep; 1465-1501 re-probes for recorded units and records an unusable manager as a scope failure; 1527-1543 refuses scope failures even after a successful portable sweep. Thus replacing the wrapper retains the distinction needed when a scoped tab outlives the cached manager verdict. Parent independently reports that g098/g101 corroborate the probe/root mapping; that corroboration is not a blanket lifecycle verdict.

Host end confirmation: host_tabs.rs:1052-1062 has a special Gone case that ends/verifies the original adopted process before forgetting the tab. Other tab closes use host_launch.rs:682-719: runtime Shutdown must report ended, otherwise it aborts the runtime and falls back to its fixed adopted process; without one it validates the socket's tag through end_host_tagged_for at 753-801. host_launch.rs:727-745 accepts only the verified process's confirmed end. A failed end retains the tab/record at host_tabs.rs:1026-1037. These source checks close the specific socket-gone versus process-gone assumption for tabs; they do not claim all host shutdown paths have been reviewed.

Restart interaction: core.rs:12719-12726 keeps the shared tab cell in restarting_tabs while the session is off-map. relaunched_entry shares session cells at 3351. Success removes the holding entry and fences the same tabs under the session map at 13183-13195; failure does so at 12911-12924. host_handover.rs:491-498 aborts those runtimes if orderly shutdown already gathered them, otherwise wakes re-adoption. An agent Restart's retained tabs therefore use the same scoped provenance and cleanup path after publication.

Detach remains infallible at the interface: core.rs:14072-14094 removes only this tab attachment, joins its forwarder and sends the tab-closed notice without a tmux command, so host_tabs.rs:999 drops no fallible result.

Suggested bucket: other; no regression established. Could-be-highest: no for the considered false-success/leftover-process and runtime-retention concerns; no newly changed destructive target or loss route was found. Confidence: confirmed for these mappings and caller contracts through source, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation of those bounded regression candidates. possible_cover: none. Caveats: host_shutdown internals and independent retained-code failure policies are not declared universally safe; l1 records the separate unchanged failed-relaunch sweep policy.
